solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 14 down, corrected here; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Flier of little importance gets auxiliary burner

parts.note: a flier who flies an aircraft is a pilot
something light is trivial, of little weight or importance

explanation.surface: An unimportant airman ends up with a back-up job in the boiler room.
explanation.definitionFit: A small permanently lit flame that ignites a gas boiler's main burner is an auxiliary burner.

clue.text: Just beats seeds

definitions.meaning: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly, so this sense is the verb form
small fruit seeds, as in an orange or apple

explanation.definitionFit: Pips narrowly beats in a race, and pips are also the small seeds in fruit like apples.

clue.text: Side's recent rule regularly ignored outside area

definitions.note: read as 'Side is', with the 's acting as a link

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late news'

indicators.note: the kept letters go around the letter for area
every other letter of the word rule is dropped, keeping the first and third

explanation.surface: A team's newly introduced regulation is only patchily enforced beyond a certain zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' leaves R and L from 'rule'; 'outside' puts them around A to give RAL, after LATE. The definition is 'Side', with 's as 'is' linking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, as in a lateral movement or a lateral thinker's sideways approach.

clue.text: One of the effects of sunblock

definitions.text: One of the effects of sunblock

parts.words: One of the effects of sunblock
parts.note: sunblock read not as a cream but as the sun itself being blocked out, by the moon passing in front

explanation.definitionFit: When the moon completely covers the sun, the event is the fullest kind of solar obscuration.

clue.text: Holy man in claim of poverty is a fraud

indicators.note: the saint's abbreviation is placed within the phrase pleading poverty

parts.note: someone pleading poverty says 'I'm poor'
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A man of God pleading poverty turns out to be a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The claim of poverty is the two-word phrase I'M POOR, which is cut open to take ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone else to deceive, so is a fraud.

clue.text: Swivelled round, missing wife, and followed like a good dog

indicators.note: the letter for wife is left out of the turning word

parts.note: to wheel is to turn or swivel around

explanation.surface: Someone spun round without their spouse, trotting along obediently like a trained dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that is told to heel walks close at its owner's heels, so a well-trained one has heeled.

clue.text: Short with no end of water? Nonsense!

indicators.note: a letter is removed from the curt word

parts.note: being short with someone is being curt or gruff

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word water is taken

explanation.surface: Someone running out of water is being brusque, and another calls it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of water' is R, which 'with no' drops from GRUFF. 'Short' is not an instruction to cut a word here but a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Guff is informal British slang for empty talk or rubbish.

clue.text: A French boss covering the centre of Paris is not listened to

parts.note: un is the French for 'a'

indicators.note: the boss word goes around the middle letter of the city

parts.note: the head of an organisation is its boss

indicators.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word Paris is taken

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's manager who oversees central Paris is ignored by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps the boss around R, which 'the centre of' picks from Paris; 'A French' is the French article, not a Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard has not been heard, so has gone unlistened to.

clue.text: Imagine pressure with no universal costume

parts.note: to fancy is to imagine or suppose

indicators.note: the letter for universal is removed from the pressure word

parts.note: duress is pressure or coercion
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Picture the strain without anything all-embracing, and you have a party outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy dress is a costume worn to dress up as a character at a party.

clue.text: Something cook may throw at people to put out

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something a cook might hurl at people to drive them away.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'at people to', ten letters rearranged; the cook throws it away, not at anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelings from potatoes are kitchen waste that a cook throws out.

clue.text: Almost consider being slim!

indicators.note: the final letter of the thinking word is dropped, leaving it nearly complete

parts.note: to think is to consider

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to consider becoming slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and slim both describe a slender person with little body fat.

clue.text: Bare minimum of crucial seconds needed for openers?

parts.note: a skeleton staff or service is the bare minimum
key means crucial, as in a key moment

explanation.surface: Asking what scant essentials of vital time are needed for opening moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeleton keys are master keys that open many locks, so they are openers.

clue.text: Lesson starting late means test!

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped, so the word starts later than usual

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A class beginning behind schedule signals that an exam is on.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a test conducted by speaking.

clue.text: Say something simple in bar that's illegal

parts.note: to say something is to speak
easy means simple

explanation.surface: Saying something straightforward in a bar that operates outside the law.
explanation.walkthrough: A speakeasy was an illicit drinking den in Prohibition-era America.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was an illicit drinking establishment during US Prohibition.

clue.text: Take in meal as it is prepared

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new order, as a meal is prepared

explanation.surface: Eat the meal just as it has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes 'is', giving ten letters; 'Take in' looks like eating but means absorb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assimilate is to absorb or take in, such as food or information.

clue.text: Person who might pick tight corset the Parisian wears

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the French article inside it, as clothing holds its wearer
tight here means drunk, so the letters of corset are jumbled

parts.note: le is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a constricting corset that a Frenchwoman wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, scrambling the corset into SECTOR; 'wears' puts the French article inside that. 'Person who might pick' is a team picker, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks the team, as in a national cricket or football selector.

clue.text: Flier needing good cover with soldiers returning

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: the soldiers' abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A pilot needs good protection as the troops come home.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft, so it is a flier.

clue.text: Bizarre steelworker holds prisoner in the USA

indicators.note: the run of letters is held within the words Bizarre steelworker

explanation.surface: A strange steelworker takes an inmate captive in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrestee is the American term for someone taken into custody.

clue.text: Devil's music causing damage

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an air is a tune or piece of music

explanation.surface: Satan's tunes are doing harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or damage something.

clue.text: Placing action on the green

definitions.meaning: on a golf green the stroke rolling the ball towards the hole is the putt

explanation.definitionFit: Putting means placing, and putting is also the gentle golf stroke on the green.

clue.text: Objections from experts covering trial

indicators.note: the experts' word wraps around the trial word

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Complaints arise from specialists reporting on a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Protests are expressions of objection or disapproval.

clue.text: Managed, after concession on orchestra's lead singer

indicators.note: the managing word is placed after the concession
in a down clue this piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the leading letter of the orchestra word is taken

explanation.surface: A musician, having made a compromise, led the orchestra's star vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female voice range.

clue.text: Material may have bearing on a juvenile

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
a teen is a young person, a juvenile

explanation.surface: Fabric may affect how a youngster behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places S above A TEEN; 'bearing' is a compass point, not posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a glossy cotton fabric, a type of material.

clue.text: One property accepting National Trust is not willing

indicators.note: the combined word takes in the trust's abbreviation

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an estate is a landed property
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage body

explanation.surface: A country house taken over by the National Trust is reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that owns stately homes. 'not willing' looks like reluctance but means without a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a will.

clue.text: Scruff's parrot attached to pole

definitions.note: read as 'Scruff is', with the 's acting as a link

parts.note: N is the north pole
to parrot is to mimic, or ape

explanation.surface: Someone untidy's bird has been fastened to a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is a verb, not the bird; the definition is 'Scruff', with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff of the neck is the back of it, the same part of the body.

clue.text: Slough is building for storage

definitions.meaning: to slough off skin is to cast it off
a simple hut, as in a garden for tools

explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to slough off, and a shed is a simple hut for storing tools.

clue.text: A ruler, not good but of a similar nature

indicators.note: the letter for good is removed from the ruler

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch who is not virtuous, yet has a comparable character.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or alike, of a similar character.

clue.text: Destroy her last ten hives!

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks their letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: A beekeeper told to wipe out her final ten beehives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hives' looks like beehives but is the skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives is the everyday name for urticaria, an itchy skin rash like a nettle sting.

clue.text: Sources of energy drink get youth nervous

indicators.note: the first letters, where each word begins, are taken

explanation.surface: Caffeinated drinks make young people jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense, anxious and on edge.

clue.text: Got up after reporting to Roger

indicators.note: the standing word is placed after the subordinate word

parts.note: someone reporting to a manager is under them
to stand up is to get up, so stood means got up

explanation.surface: Someone rose after giving their report to a man named Roger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a name but is the radio reply meaning message received.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio talk, Roger signals that a message was received and comprehended.
